ai-workspace · gravity

Kepler & gravity — an introduction

A documentation-as-contract system for running many projects with AI coding agents — so your intent survives every session, machine, and model.

This page owns the workspace half. The protocol half travels with every project and is explained in its own browser-read guide — gravity/GRAVITY-GUIDE.html, which lands in each adopted repo as .gravity/GRAVITY.html.

01Two products, one workspace

What lives here is two things with one name between them, and keeping them apart is what makes either portable:

Kepler this machine

The workspace manager — the laws of motion for a fleet of projects: tiers, junctions, the live index, the dashboard. It never leaves this root.

gravity travels

The protocol a project adopts — the doc kinds, the domain rules, the SPEC walls, the evidence doors, the instruments. It ships inside each independent repo and works with no workspace in sight.

The name is the core metaphor: every fact has exactly one home it gravitates to, and every project carries enough mass — mission, rules, plan — that agents orbit it correctly instead of drifting.

Neither half is a framework you install. They are disciplines with mechanical backing: templates you copy, indexes that must stay wired, enforcement tags that must be honest, and checkers (check.py, /triage) that catch the drift for you.

02The problem it solves

Agent sessions are powerful and amnesiac. Between sessions, machines, and model generations, three things evaporate:

  • State — where was I? what's next? (the resume problem)
  • Rules — what must never break here? which conventions are real walls vs. taste? (the safety problem)
  • Intent — why does this exist? what are we deliberately not doing? (the direction problem)

No model, however capable, can re-derive choices — non-goals, locked decisions, boundary contracts. They exist only in your head or in a chat that scrolled away. Gravity is a persistence layer for that judgment: each concern gets one document, at one rate of change, loaded at the right moment.

03The workspace

One root, four tiers, one index. Projects live in repos/ (storage); tier folders hold junctions (views) — moving a project between tiers is instant metadata, never a file copy.

ai-workspace/
├── CLAUDE.md            # the operating manual — auto-loads, the one router
├── PROJECTS.md          # live index: every project, tier, focus, gravity adoption
├── VERSION · CHANGELOG.md  # gravity itself is versioned (see §06)
├── docs/ · gravity/templates/ · .claude/   # read-docs · stencils · commands + scripts
├── repos/               # CANONICAL storage — real project files, one folder per project
└── active/ · stable/ · dormant/ · archive/   # junction views: being worked · works · paused · over

The root repo tracks only the skeleton (deny-all .gitignore, whitelist the meta files) — each project is its own independent git repo. A project is the unit of attention, not the unit of git: a project usually holds one repo, but a multi-service system can be a hub project — a docs-only repo with the service clones nested inside, git-denied.

04The protocol, in one screen

Everything below travels inside the project repo, so it keeps working in a clone that has never seen this workspace. One line each here; the full treatment — with diagrams and a phrasebook of what to ask an agent for — is the guide.

The ruleIn one line
Four clocksDocs are split by rate of change — mission (rarely) · CLAUDE.md (on refactors) · plan (per phase) · CONTEXT.md (per session). Mixing rates is what makes docs rot. Two auto-load; the rest are recognized only when present.
One concern, one homeEvery fact has exactly one owner-doc; every other doc links to it instead of restating it. The same fact written twice eventually becomes two different facts.
Domains, not doc-typesHeavy docs live in .gravity/<domain>/, one folder per subject. The directory is the registry — no registry file — and a leading _ marks gravity's own machinery, never a domain.
SPECs are wallsA domain's SPEC.md is a Minimal Shape to build from plus enforcement-tagged Rules that fence it. A rule nothing enforces says [review] or [—] rather than pretending.
Direction earns a homeA principle becomes a Track, a Track becomes slices, and slices leave residue as SPEC rules — at which point the Track retires. An unowned wish rots, so gravity refuses to store one.
Three evidence doorsBug reports (the past), handed-in knowledge, and agreed requirements (the future) all enter as cited text before anything is planned — so a claim months later still traces to who said it.
Brownfield inverts the orderOn a system you did not write, the integration domain comes first: a Boundary Map where every row cites its source file, and a seam that cannot be traced stays an honest OPEN:.
The protocol ships in two voices. Every adopted repo carries .gravity/GRAVITY.md — the card, the canonical version written for the agent — and .gravity/GRAVITY.html — the guide, the same protocol written for the engineer who just opened the repo. They are copied verbatim at adoption and refreshed together; only the card carries the version stamp. Read the guide at gravity/GRAVITY-GUIDE.html, or open any adopted project's copy.

05The lifecycle & commands

MomentCommandWhat it does
start / ship/init-project · /shipscaffold a new project · move a shipped one to the stable orbit
seed intent/interviewelicit why/walls/shape/gate/next from your head into the docs — strawman-first, unknowns stay OPEN:
structure/adopt-gravity · /new-domain · /new-specmove onto .gravity/ · mint a domain (all four indexes wired) · author an honest SPEC from code evidence
legacy/excavatesurvey a brownfield system; cited Boundary Map + domain proposal
steer/mission · /triage · /dashboard · /observatoryre-orient on one project · drift report across all · the per-project observatory
ship/cut-releaseone Change Order: changelog → version → commit → tag; never invents a version, never tags red code
stay current/sync-gravitybring a project up to the current gravity version — mechanical parts applied, judgment reported as a checklist
end/retirearchive (reversible) or delete (permanent), with a risk card first

Gravity tests its own commands: .claude/scenarios/ holds golden fixtures with deterministic assertions, and check.py selftest proves the checkers themselves.

06Gravity is versioned

The methodology itself follows SemVer — major = a rule projects depend on breaks. The version lives in the VERSION file + a git tag, never in prose. Each project records what it adopted in two stamps: the > gravity: vX.Y line in its router and the protocol card's stamp — so stale adoptions are visible (adoption table in PROJECTS.md, chips on the dashboard, 📡 in /triage) and repairable (/sync-gravity).

07The philosophy

  • Weaker-agent walls. Wherever judgment can fail, build a mechanical wall instead: argv-driven scripts, verbatim copies, versions that are read, never invented. The system is designed so a less capable agent can't fabricate enforcement — and a more capable one doesn't have to be trusted.
  • Honesty over completeness. An unknown is an OPEN: line, not a plausible guess. An unenforced rule is [review], not a fake wall. A partial evidence pack is a valid state.
  • Ceremony must pay. Two docs are the minimum and often the maximum. Everything else is recognized only when present, gated by ambition, and deleted when it stops earning its keep.
  • Intent is the scarce resource. Models get stronger and code gets cheaper; your decisions, non-goals, and boundaries do not regenerate. Gravity exists to make those durable — and to apply them automatically to work you'll never personally watch.
